                  <ns0:p n="12">12 Gather the people together <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Not into one place, where all could not hear, but into di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vers Assemblies or Synagogues.</ns0:note>, men, and wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />men <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Who hereby are required to go to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> at this solemnity, as they were permitted to do in other solemnities, when the Males onely were enjoyned to go, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 23. 17.</ns0:note>, and children <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">To wit, such of them as could understand, as appears from <ns0:hi>Neh.</ns0:hi> 8. 2, 3.</ns0:note>, and thy stranger <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) The Proselytes, though others also were admitted.</ns0:note> that <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">That they may then certainly and constantly do so, though they had also other opportunities to do so, as upon the Sabbath-days, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 15. 21. and other solemn feasts, yea even in their private houses.</ns0:note>, and fear the LORD your God, and observe to do all the words of this law:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> their children which have not known <ns0:hi>any thing,</ns0:hi> may hear and learn to fear the LORD your God, as long as ye live in the land, whither ye go over Jordan to possess it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And the LORD said unto Moses, Behold, thy dayes approach that thou must die: call Joshua, and present your selves in the tabernacle <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Either properly so called, for though the Priests onely might ordinarily enter there, yet others might go in upon a call and command from God, which here they had: or in the court of the Tabernacle, at the door of which God stood in the cloudy pillar, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15. the Court coming here under the name of the <ns0:hi>Tabernacle,</ns0:hi> as elsewhere it comes under the name of the <ns0:hi>Temple.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> of the congregation, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 27. 19.</ns0:note> I may give him a charge <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Immediately from my self for his greater encouragement, and to gain him more authority with the people.</ns0:note>. And Moses and Joshua went and presented them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves in the tabernacle of the congregation.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 33. 9.</ns0:note> the LORD appeared in the taberna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cle, in a pillar of a cloud: and the pillar of the cloud, stood over the door of the tabernacle.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 And the LORD said unto Moses, Behold, thou shalt <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> lie down.</ns0:note> sleep <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The death of men, both good and bad, is oft called a <ns0:hi>sleep,</ns0:hi> because they shall certainly awake out of it by resurrection. See <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 76. 5. <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 12. 2. 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 4. 13, &c. 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3. 4.</ns0:note> with thy fathers, and this peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple will rise up, and go a whoring <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">God certainly foresees all things to come, yea, even those which de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pend upon the wills of men, or contingencies of the things, as this unquestionably did.</ns0:note> after the gods of the strangers of the land <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Of the <ns0:hi>Canaanites,</ns0:hi> who now are possessours, but shortly will be turned out of their possessions, and become as strangers in their own land.                   <ns0:p n="17">17 Then my anger shall be kindled against them in that day, and I will forsake them, and I will <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 104. 29.</ns0:note> hide my face <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Withdraw my favour and help.</ns0:note> from them, and they shall be de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />voured, and many evils and troubles shall  befall<ns0:note n="†" place="margin"> Heb. <ns0:hi>

                           </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> them, so that they will say in that day, Are not these evils come upon us, because our God <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> not amongst us?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 And I will surely hide my face in that day, for all the evils which they shall have wrought, in that they are turned unto other gods.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 Now therefore write ye this song <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Which is contained <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32. and is put into a song that it be better learned, and more fixed in their minds and memories.</ns0:note> for you<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and teach it the children of Israel, put it in their mouths <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Cause them to learn it, and sing it one to another, to oblige them to more circumspection and watchfulness.</ns0:note>, that this song may be a witness for me <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Of my kind<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness in giving them so many blessings, of my patience in bear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing so long with them, of my clemency in giving them such fair and plain warnings, and my justice in punishing such an un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thankful perverse and incorrigible people.</ns0:note> against the children of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 For when I shall have brought them into the land which I sware unto their fathers, that flow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth with milk and honey, and they shall have eaten and filled themselves, and waxen fat; <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 6. 10 &c and 8. 10. and 32. 15.</ns0:note> then will they turn unto other gods, and serve them, and provoke me, and break my covenant.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And it shall come to pass, when many evils and<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> troubles are befallen them, that this song shall testifie <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> before.</ns0:note> against them as a witness: for it shall not be forgotten <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">This seems not to be a precept that they should remember it, but a prediction, that God would give them sad occasion to remember it, by bringing upon them the dreadful calamities mentioned in it.</ns0:note> out of the mouths of their seed: for I know their imagination, which they <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> do.</ns0:note> go about even now <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Either their inward inclinations to Idola<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />try, which they do not check, as they ought, but rather enter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain with delight, and some of them do not onely cherish it in their hearts, but as far as they can and dare, secretly practise it, as may be gathered from <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> 5. 25. <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 7. 43. or their se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cret purposes to allow themselves therein, when they are set<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tled in their land, which were clearly known to God, though it may be not fully evident to themselves.</ns0:note>, before I have brought them into the land which I sware.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 Moses therefore wrote this song the same day, and taught it the children of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 And he gave Joshua the son of Nun a charge and said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Josh. 1. 6.</ns0:note> Be strong and of a good courage: for thou shalt bring the children of Israel into the land which I sware unto them <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">This wickedness of theirs which I now foresee and foretell shall not hinder me from bringing them into <ns0:hi>Canaan.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: and I will be with thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 And it came to pass, when Moses had made an end of writing the words of this law in a book, until they were finished;</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">25 That Moses commanded the Levites <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) The Priests <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 9. who also were <ns0:hi>Levites.</ns0:hi>

Here it was kept for greater security and reverence.</ns0:note> of the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, that it may be there for a witness a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst thee <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Against thy people, to whom he here turns his speech that they might be more affected with it.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 For I know thy rebellion, and thy stiff-neck; behold, while I am yet alive with you this day, ye have been rebellious against the LORD, and how much more after my death?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 Gather unto me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, that I may speak these words in their ears, and call heaven and earth to record a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst them.</ns0:p>
